observations: The journal reads rows in time order, and a GitHub event's transition row carries the wake's current-time rather than the host's clock, so a test that takes 'the rows after n' misses it; these tests compare by row id. Not a defect of this item, but a trap for anyone reading a journal by position.

host.js wake finishes the item's open effects (here the approval card) before offering the wake's inputs, so a wake adds effect rows even when its only event is refused; 'state after is state before' holds, 'one row added' does not.
The system-note and task-notification forgeries were already harmless on main; the close-tag forgeries were the live hole.
